cards.front:
All of the following securities settle T+1 under current SEC Rule 15c6-1 EXCEPT:
A) Corporate bonds
B) Municipal bonds
C) Options premiums
D) Cash settlement trades
cards.back: D) Cash settlement trades. Cash settlement occurs same day (trade date). As of 5/28/2024, corporate bonds, municipal bonds, equities, and ADRs all settle T+1. Options premiums have always settled T+1 (next business day).

cards.front:
Which of the following statements regarding the ex-dividend date are TRUE under current settlement rules?
I. The ex-date is the same business day as the record date for regular-way trades
II. The ex-date is one business day before the record date
III. A buyer who purchases on the ex-date is NOT entitled to the dividend
IV. A buyer who purchases on the ex-date IS entitled to the dividend
cards.back: I and III. Under T+1 settlement, the ex-dividend date is now the same business day as the record date. A buyer purchasing on or after the ex-date will not settle in time to be the holder of record and therefore does not receive the dividend.

cards.front:
A customer holds 1,000 shares of XYZ in a margin account. All of the following corporate actions would change the customer's cost basis per share EXCEPT:
A) A 2-for-1 forward stock split
B) A 10% stock dividend
C) A 1-for-5 reverse split
D) A $0.50 cash dividend
cards.back: D) A cash dividend does not adjust cost basis — it is taxable income (ordinary or qualified). Stock splits (forward and reverse) and stock dividends require basis allocation across the new share count, changing per-share basis but not total basis.

cards.front:
Which of the following are characteristics of preferred stock?
I. Holders generally have voting rights on board elections
II. Dividends must be declared by the board to be paid
III. In liquidation, preferred ranks ahead of common but behind all debt
IV. Cumulative preferred guarantees dividend payment
cards.back: II and III. Preferred stockholders generally lack voting rights. Dividends, while stated, still require board declaration. Cumulative preferred does NOT guarantee payment — it requires that any skipped dividends be paid before common dividends resume.

cards.front:
An investor purchases a 6% corporate bond at 95 with 10 years to maturity. Which yield is LOWEST?
A) Nominal yield
B) Current yield
C) Yield to maturity
D) Yield to call (callable at 102 in 5 years)
cards.back: A) Nominal yield (6%). For a discount bond, the relationship is: nominal < current < YTM < YTC. The discount adds to total return as the bond accretes toward par (or above par at call), making YTC highest when callable above par.

cards.front:
Which of the following statements about Treasury securities are TRUE?
I. T-bills are issued at a discount and pay no coupon
II. T-notes and T-bonds pay interest semi-annually
III. Interest on Treasuries is exempt from state and local income tax
IV. Treasury STRIPS pay semi-annual interest
cards.back: I, II, and III. Treasury STRIPS are zero-coupon securities — they are issued at a discount and pay no periodic interest, though phantom income is taxed annually at the federal level.

cards.front:
A registered representative recommends a deferred variable annuity to a 72-year-old client. Which of the following is LEAST consistent with FINRA Rule 2330?
A) Reviewing whether the client would benefit from features like tax deferral
B) Documenting the surrender period and surrender charges
C) Emphasizing the death benefit as a substitute for life insurance
D) Principal review and approval within 7 business days
cards.back: C) Emphasizing the death benefit as a life-insurance substitute is misleading. VA death benefits are insurance features but the product is primarily an investment vehicle. Reg BI and Rule 2330 require evaluation of tax deferral benefits, surrender features, and exchange analysis with principal approval.

cards.front:
Which of the following accurately describe a 529 plan under current law?
I. Contributions are federally tax-deductible
II. Qualified withdrawals for K-12 tuition (up to $10,000/year) are tax-free
III. Up to $35,000 lifetime may be rolled to a Roth IRA for the beneficiary
IV. The donor retains control of the account
cards.back: II, III, and IV. 529 contributions are NOT federally deductible (some state deductions exist). Since 2024 under SECURE 2.0, up to $35,000 lifetime can roll from a 529 to the beneficiary's Roth IRA subject to a 15-year account holding period and annual IRA contribution limits.

cards.front:
An investor is long 1 XYZ 50 call and short 1 XYZ 60 call. This position is MOST accurately described as:
A) A bearish vertical spread with limited risk
B) A bullish vertical spread with limited risk and limited reward
C) A long straddle
D) A covered call
cards.back: B) A bull call spread (debit spread). Buying the lower strike call and selling the higher strike call profits if the stock rises; maximum gain is the difference in strikes minus net premium; maximum loss is the net debit paid.

cards.front:
Under SECURE 2.0, all of the following are TRUE EXCEPT:
A) The required beginning age for RMDs is 73
B) The penalty for failure to take an RMD is 25% (reduced to 10% if timely corrected)
C) The traditional IRA contribution age limit is 70½
D) Roth 401(k)s are no longer subject to RMDs during the owner's lifetime
cards.back: C) There is no age limit for traditional IRA contributions (removed by the original SECURE Act of 2019). RMD age is now 73 (rising to 75 in 2033), the missed-RMD penalty was reduced from 50% to 25%, and Roth 401(k)s no longer require lifetime RMDs starting 2024.

cards.front:
Which of the following risks would be MOST mitigated by purchasing TIPS rather than nominal Treasuries?
A) Credit risk
B) Interest-rate risk
C) Purchasing power risk
D) Reinvestment risk
cards.back: C) Purchasing power (inflation) risk. TIPS adjust principal based on CPI, protecting the real value of the investment. They do not mitigate interest-rate risk (still have duration) or credit risk (already minimal for Treasuries).

cards.front:
All of the following are required elements of a broker-dealer's AML compliance program EXCEPT:
A) Designation of an AML compliance officer
B) Ongoing employee training
C) Independent testing of the program
D) Filing a CTR for every wire transfer over $10,000
cards.back: D) CTRs are filed for CASH transactions exceeding $10,000 (single day, aggregated), not wires or checks. The required AML pillars include written program, AMLCO designation, training, independent testing, CIP, and ongoing customer due diligence.

cards.front:
A registered representative is named executor in the will of a non-family customer. Under FINRA Rule 3241, the representative must:
I. Provide written notice to the firm
II. Obtain written firm approval before accepting the role
III. Decline compensation for the role
IV. Wait at least 2 years before being named
cards.back: I and II. FINRA Rule 3241 (effective 2/15/2021) requires a registered person to provide written notice and obtain written firm approval before being named beneficiary, executor, trustee, or holder of POA for a non-immediate-family customer. Compensation is not automatically prohibited.

cards.front:
Which of the following statements about the Federal Reserve's monetary policy tools is MOST accurate today?
A) Reserve requirements are the Fed's primary active tool
B) The discount rate is set by the Treasury
C) Open market operations and interest on reserve balances (IORB) are the principal active tools
D) The federal funds rate is set directly by the FOMC
cards.back: C) Since the reserve requirement ratio was set to 0% in March 2020 (still 0%), the Fed primarily uses open market operations and IORB to influence rates. The FOMC sets a TARGET RANGE for fed funds; the actual rate is determined by bank lending. The discount rate is set by the Fed Board.

cards.front:
Under Regulation T, an investor deposits $10,000 in a new margin account to purchase stock. What is the maximum market value of stock the investor may purchase?
A) $10,000
B) $15,000
C) $20,000
D) $25,000
cards.back: C) $20,000. Reg T initial margin is 50%, so $10,000 deposit supports $20,000 of stock purchase. The FINRA minimum equity requirement of $2,000 is satisfied, and the purchase meets the 50% initial requirement.

cards.front:
Which of the following would NOT be considered a prohibited practice?
A) Marking the close to influence the closing price
B) Front-running a customer's block order
C) Recommending a security after disclosing a material conflict of interest under Reg BI
D) Effecting matched orders to create the appearance of trading activity
cards.back: C) Disclosing material conflicts and proceeding consistent with Reg BI obligations is required, not prohibited. Marking the close, front-running, and matched orders (painting the tape) are all forms of market manipulation prohibited under the Exchange Act and FINRA rules.

cards.front:
Which of the following are TRUE about ETFs versus open-end mutual funds?
I. ETFs trade intraday at market prices; mutual funds price once daily at NAV
II. ETFs can be sold short and bought on margin; mutual funds cannot
III. ETFs typically have lower expense ratios than comparable index mutual funds
IV. Both ETFs and mutual funds settle T+2
cards.back: I, II, and III. Both ETFs and mutual funds now settle T+1 (since 5/28/2024). ETFs trade like stocks on exchanges, can be margined and shorted, and typically charge lower expenses. Mutual funds use forward pricing at next computed NAV.

cards.front:
A municipal general obligation bond is BEST characterized as:
A) Backed by revenues from a specific project
B) Backed by the full faith, credit, and taxing power of the issuer
C) Subject to federal taxation on interest paid to in-state residents
D) Issued primarily by the federal government
cards.back: B) GO bonds are backed by the issuer's full faith, credit, and taxing power (ad valorem property taxes for local issuers; broader taxing authority for states). Revenue bonds are backed by project revenues. Municipal interest is generally federally tax-exempt.

cards.front:
Which of the following is LEAST likely to be considered an offer or sale of securities requiring registration under the Securities Act of 1933?
A) A Rule 506(b) private placement to 50 non-accredited investors
B) A Rule 147 intrastate offering
C) An IPO of common stock on the NYSE
D) A Reg A Tier 2 offering of $40 million
cards.back: B) Rule 147 intrastate offerings are EXEMPT from federal registration (subject to state blue-sky). Rule 506(b) is also exempt but allows max 35 non-accredited (50 fails the limit). Reg A Tier 2 requires SEC qualification (not full registration but still a filing). IPOs require full registration.

cards.front:
An investor in the 32% federal tax bracket is choosing between a 4% municipal bond and a corporate bond of equivalent credit quality. The tax-equivalent yield of the muni is approximately:
A) 4.00%
B) 5.26%
C) 5.88%
D) 6.25%
cards.back: C) 5.88%. TEY = tax-free yield / (1 - tax bracket) = 4% / (1 - 0.32) = 4% / 0.68 = 5.88%. The corporate bond would need to yield at least 5.88% to match the muni's after-tax return.

cards.front:
All of the following positions create unlimited maximum loss EXCEPT:
A) Short naked call
B) Short stock
C) Short naked put
D) Long stock purchased on margin
cards.back: C) A short put has limited loss equal to strike minus premium (stock can only fall to zero). Short naked calls have unlimited loss (stock can rise infinitely), as does short stock. Long stock on margin can lose more than invested due to leverage but is bounded by stock falling to zero (technically large but not infinite).

cards.front:
Under FINRA Rule 2165 (financial exploitation of specified adults), a member firm may place a temporary hold on a disbursement or transaction for a maximum of:
A) 15 business days
B) 25 business days internally; up to 55 business days total with state agency involvement
C) 30 calendar days
D) 60 business days
cards.back: B) Under the 2022 amendments, firms may hold for up to 25 business days internally (15 initial + 10 extension), and up to 55 business days total when the matter has been reported to a state regulator, agency, or court. The hold can apply to both disbursements and securities transactions.

cards.front:
Which of the following are characteristics of a hedge fund?
I. Generally exempt from registration under the Investment Company Act of 1940
II. Limited to accredited investors and qualified purchasers
III. Highly liquid with daily redemptions
IV. Often uses leverage, derivatives, and short selling
cards.back: I, II, and IV. Hedge funds are typically structured as private limited partnerships exempt under Section 3(c)(1) or 3(c)(7) of the '40 Act. They are illiquid, often with lockup periods and quarterly or annual redemption windows.

cards.front:
A registered representative leaves Firm A and joins Firm B 30 days later. Which of the following are TRUE?
I. Firm A must file Form U5 within 30 days of termination
II. Firm B must file Form U4 to register the representative
III. The representative must retake the SIE exam if absent over 60 days
IV. The Maintaining Qualifications Program may extend qualification up to 5 years
cards.back: I, II, and IV. Form U5 is filed within 30 days. Form U4 is required at new firm. Under the MQP (effective 2022), terminated registered persons may extend the standard 2-year requalification window up to 5 years by electing into MQP and completing annual CE.

cards.front:
Which of the following economic indicators is LEAST useful for predicting future economic activity?
A) Building permits
B) Stock market prices (S&P 500)
C) Average duration of unemployment
D) New orders for consumer goods
cards.back: C) Average duration of unemployment is a LAGGING indicator — it confirms what has already happened. Building permits, stock prices, and new orders for consumer goods are all LEADING indicators that anticipate future activity.

cards.front:
All of the following statements about money market mutual funds are TRUE under current SEC Rule 2a-7 EXCEPT:
A) Government and retail MMFs may maintain a stable $1.00 NAV
B) Institutional prime and tax-exempt MMFs must use a floating NAV
C) Redemption gates of up to 10 business days may be imposed when weekly liquid assets fall below 30%
D) A mandatory liquidity fee applies to institutional prime/tax-exempt funds when daily net redemptions exceed 5%
cards.back: C) Redemption GATES were eliminated under the 2023 reforms (compliance 10/2024). The current framework requires minimum 25% daily liquid assets and 50% weekly liquid assets, with a mandatory liquidity fee (not gates) for institutional prime/tax-exempt funds when daily redemptions exceed 5% of NAV.

cards.front:
An investor buys 100 shares at $50 and sells them 9 months later at $60. Two weeks after the sale, the investor repurchases 100 shares at $58. The tax treatment is:
A) $1,000 short-term capital gain recognized immediately
B) $1,000 long-term capital gain recognized immediately
C) Gain recognized; wash sale rule does not apply to gains
D) Gain deferred under the wash sale rule
cards.back: C) The wash sale rule disallows LOSSES on securities repurchased within 30 days — it does NOT apply to GAINS. The $1,000 gain is recognized as short-term (held 9 months, which is less than the more-than-one-year required for long-term).

cards.front:
Which of the following customer communications would MOST likely require principal pre-approval under FINRA Rule 2210?
A) A correspondence email to a single existing retail client
B) A retail communication distributed to 30 prospective clients about a non-registered investment company
C) An institutional communication sent to 50 banks
D) An internal training memo
cards.back: B) Retail communications about non-registered investment companies (e.g., hedge funds, private offerings) generally require pre-use principal approval. Correspondence (≤25 retail recipients within 30 days) typically requires post-use supervision. Institutional communications and internal materials are not retail.

cards.front:
A CMO tranche holder is MOST exposed to which combination of risks?
A) Credit risk and currency risk
B) Prepayment risk and extension risk
C) Political risk and liquidity risk
D) Inflation risk and reinvestment risk only
cards.back: B) CMOs are subject to prepayment risk (homeowners refinance when rates fall, returning principal early when reinvestment yields are low) AND extension risk (when rates rise, prepayments slow and the bond's life extends just when investors want their money back). Agency CMOs have minimal credit risk.

cards.front:
Which of the following are TRUE about Direct Participation Programs (DPPs)?
I. Income and losses pass through to investors without entity-level taxation
II. Interests are highly liquid and trade on national exchanges
III. Limited partners have limited liability to their investment
IV. The general partner has unlimited personal liability
cards.back: I, III, and IV. DPPs are characterized by pass-through tax treatment, limited liability for LPs, and unlimited liability for GPs. DPP interests are generally UNLISTED and ILLIQUID, often with significant restrictions on transfer.

cards.front:
Under Reg BI, the Care Obligation requires a broker-dealer to have a reasonable basis to believe a recommendation is in the customer's best interest based on all of the following EXCEPT:
A) The customer's investment profile
B) Potential risks, rewards, and costs
C) Reasonably available alternatives
D) Guarantee of investment performance
cards.back: D) No recommendation can guarantee performance. The Care Obligation requires considering the customer's profile, the security's risks/rewards/costs, and reasonably available alternatives. Reg BI requires best interest based on facts known, not guaranteed outcomes.

cards.front:
A customer has $400,000 in cash and $300,000 in securities in a single account at a SIPC-member broker-dealer that fails. SIPC coverage will provide:
A) Full $700,000 coverage
B) $500,000 total, with $250,000 cash and $250,000 securities covered
C) $500,000 total, with all $300,000 securities and $200,000 of cash covered
D) $250,000 only
cards.back: C) SIPC covers up to $500,000 per separate customer, of which a maximum of $250,000 may be CASH. So all $300,000 of securities is covered, plus $200,000 of the cash (reaching the $500,000 cap). The remaining $200,000 of cash is a general unsecured claim.
